paper.title_en: An optical-frequency-comb-enabled unified infrastructure for quantum networks
paper.abstract_en: Quantum networks require precision timing and classical communication to coordinate distributed quantum operations, yet these functions are typically supported by separate infrastructures, increasing system complexity and limiting scalability. Here we demonstrate an optical-frequency-comb-enabled infrastructure that unifies precision timing, classical communication and quantum communication over a shared fibre link. By encoding classical data onto the intensity of the comb while retaining its pulse timing, we simultaneously transmit data at 100 Mbit/s and achieve a timing stability of 0.85 fs at 1 s over 100 km. We develop a spectral-engineering strategy to suppress the coupling between data modulation and timing extraction. We further establish a power-dependent model of the excess noise induced in a co-propagating continuous-variable quantum key distribution channel, identifying optical power, wavelength allocation and propagation direction as the principal control parameters. After optimization, the system introduces only 0.0037 shot noise unit of additional excess noise and limits the secret-key-rate penalty to 6.7%. Furthermore, quantum-secured timestamp transmission additionally enables absolute time synchronization with a stability of 0.26 fs at 1 s. These results establish optical frequency combs as a common physical layer for integrated quantum-network services.
